question: Does a stock-quoted launch hide exit cost in leg2 (token->xStock->USDC) that pool pages do not show?
verdict: NO — not as a headline differentiator
summary: Across 6 measured stock-quoted launches (STONK/SPYx, SNP500/SPYx, FTR/TSLAx, NVDGE/NVDAx, FRIES/MCDx, ROB/HOODx), the hidden leg2 tax is under 1% at every size where exit is possible. Leg1 (token->quote stock) and full cash exit track together. The binding constraint is almost always the meme/launch pool (leg1), not converting the quote stock to USDC (leg2).
what_actually_hurts: Printed mcap vs executable cash exit (STONK: $215M mcap but $1M exit recovers only 85%)
Leg1 pool depth on the launch pair, not quote-stock conversion
No-route walls on thin launches (FTR fails above $25k; NVDGE above $100k)
Ticker impersonation on quote and base assets
revised_product_focus: Cash exit curve per launch (not leg1-only pool page view)
Identify binding leg: leg1 vs leg2 vs no-route

hoodx_direct_stress_test.note: HOODx->USDC direct, no meme leg. Leg2 only becomes material above $250k.
